Behavior Layer

Components

Components add reusable behavior to Actors through composition rather than inheritance.

Core Idea

Keep Actors light. Attach the behaviors you need. This makes systems modular, testable, and easy to combine.

For authored Fragments, Root Core Components are shared by Player, AI, and future commander profiles. Acceleration, Pitch, Yaw, and Barrel Roll can therefore be authored once in Core when every controller should use the same flight model. Player keyboard and mouse bindings remain in the Player Input Manager; any controller can produce the logical input channels those Components consume.

Homing Projectiles

Weapon homing is opt-in for compatibility. Enable Homing Enabled and set Homing Turn Rate in degrees per second to make each fired projectile steer toward the target selected at launch.

Homing Off

The projectile keeps its launch direction and expires at the authored Range endpoint. Existing weapons and legacy records use this behavior.

Homing On

The projectile turns toward its captured target at no more than the authored turn rate. Range still controls whether the weapon may engage, but does not expire the projectile after launch.

If the target is destroyed or removed, the missile continues unguided for up to 0.75 seconds before cleanup. A hidden 15-second safety ceiling prevents orphaned projectiles. Hit Boxes currently refine impact on the intended target; flares and interception volumes are separate future countermeasure behavior.

Tag

Adds authored labels to a Fragment for identification and filtering by gameplay or scripts.

Resource

Creates tracked values such as Health, with a maximum and starting value for damage and other systems.

Team

Assigns faction ownership used by team colors, targeting, damage rules, and match logic.

Targeting

Searches for valid targets within a configured radius, optionally requiring an enemy team. Autonomous targeting respects authored scan categories: ordinary placed Buildings are targetable Structures, while placed roots with Gameplay Role None are ignored even if they have resources. It can show a tinted warning line from its host to the current target before a weapon fires.

Hit Box

Provides optional rendered-surface hit geometry for more precise projectile impacts. Its editor wireframe is diagnostic only and does not change the Fragment's physical collider or targeting rules.

Weapon

Fires from an authored input channel with damage, range, projectile speed, optional homing, and cooldown settings. Range is the maximum projectile travel distance and forward crosshair endpoint for normal shots; Projectile Speed controls travel speed. Homing is off by default and uses a bounded Homing Turn Rate when enabled. Target acquisition belongs to Targeting and Auto Combat. It can use muzzle anchors, projectile visuals, muzzle flashes, and a local crosshair.

Lane Push

Moves an AI unit along the active lane, turns toward its route, and can pause for combat while staying on the authored plane.

Acceleration

Reads a signed local input channel and accelerates or decelerates forward movement up to the configured response rates.

Pitch

Reads a signed local input channel and smoothly turns the Fragment around its pitch axis.

Yaw

Reads a signed local input channel and smoothly turns the Fragment around its yaw axis.

Barrel Roll

Reads one signed input channel and continuously rolls the Fragment around its forward axis while the input is held. Positive and Negative / Opposite controls are combined by the Player Profile binding; the sign selects the roll direction. Sensitivity controls the roll rate, and releasing the input stops the roll.

Rotating Movement

Provides UE-style continuous rotation from authored X, Y, and Z rates in degrees per second. Local Space composes the rate in the host's local frame; disabling it applies the rate in world space relative to the immediate parent. It can be placed on a Fragment root or Anchor and previews in the Wings Assembler.

Auto Combat

Turns the host toward the current Targeting result and requests attacks from Weapon without player input. Aim Speed and optional reaction time control response; Weapon still owns cooldown and projectile delivery.

Auto Input

Emits a local input channel at a configured interval when its range conditions are met, allowing weapons and other listeners to react.

Spawn

Marks an authored Fragment as able to participate in the Fragment spawn path used by runtime gameplay.

Player Start

Marks a Fragment Root or Anchor as a team-owned player start. PlayerStart selection uses the placed Fragment’s inherited team and authored transform.

Particle Emitter

Attaches a particle asset to the authored host and optionally starts it automatically during runtime.

Respawn

Returns an Actor to its initial spawn context after destruction or a configured respawn input, with an authored delay.

Unknown

Preserves an unrecognized component definition so newer or custom data is not discarded when an older editor loads and saves the Fragment.

Authoring

ComponentDefinitions on FragmentAssets describe intended behavior. Root Core definitions are shared by the active controller profile; Player and AI profiles specialize behavior; and supported Anchor definitions localize behavior at the Anchor transform. At runtime they are turned into live Component instances on Actors. Mesh nodes remain visual-only.

Best Practice

Prefer small, focused Components. Compose them to create complex behavior instead of large monolithic classes.
